title: Datastream, Data Transfer Service and change data capture

videos.script: Quitanda's reports still read the shop's own PostgreSQL, and orders arrive in it every minute. Moving that data is the problem of this lesson. {{shop}} Copying the tables takes hours, and the shop will not stop for hours. So there are two halves. Copy what is there, then keep up with what keeps changing. {{halves}} The second half is change data capture. Every database writes its changes to a log before it applies them, and CDC reads that log from outside. {{log}} Datastream does both halves, into BigQuery or a bucket. Database Migration Service does them when the database itself is moving. {{services}} Neither has an emulator. So you will run the real thing: a PostgreSQL server on your machine, a publication, a replication slot, and the changes coming out as you make them. {{slot}} You will also see the slot's danger. Stop reading it, and the database keeps its log until the disk fills, or until a ceiling throws the slot away. {{danger}} And at the end, the cutover in the order that loses nothing, and what the changes cost by the gibibyte. {{end}}
